messages:
Ivy (marketing): Need a compact battlecard + two-slide webinar hook focused on serving economics vs cloud endpoints and infra vendors. Keep bullets tight.
Dan (sales): Field wins: predictable bills, fallback safety, and incremental migration. Need one-line rebuttals.
Rex (product): Structure: claim (1 line), why it matters (1 line), demo hook (1 line). Add a micro-technical footnote for SREs.
Maya (eng): Bench note: internal dialogue tests show ~2x median token cost reduction with KV prefix caching + continuous batching vs a leading managed endpoint; label as internal lab results. Avoid global p99 claims.
Ivy (marketing): Draft hero lines: "Keep your models. Fix your inference economics." or "Serve smarter: stable latency, lower unit cost."
Dan (sales): Objection/reply quick pairs:
 - Obj: "We're already on CloudProd."
   Reply: "CloudProd is great for dev. At scale teams hit opaque bill spikes and tail latency; Redwood adds routing, caching and fallbacks so bills and SLOs are predictable."
 - Obj: "Migration is too heavy."
   Reply: "Start with our API as a drop-in and enable routing/caching incrementally; dedicated/private installs available for lift-and-shift."
Rex (product): SRE micro-line: "Continuous coalescing, per-session KV prefix reuse, and model-variant routing reduce repeated compute while preserving median latency."
Maya (eng): Tiny routing policy for slide:
`{"policy":"latency-first","fallbacks":["lite-quant"],"kv_cache":true,"batch_target_ms":8}`
Ivy (marketing): Inbound routing rules (short): keywords->AE: "SLA|on-prem|private|dedicated|compliance"; keywords->SDR: "trial|signup|api key|embed|free credits"; score>=80->AE,50-79->SDR,<50->mkt drip.
asset-bot: Created asset stub https://internal.redwood/marketing/assets/serve-strike-brief (permissions: marketing-edit).
Dan (sales): I'll add two roleplay snippets after Ivy drops the one-pager.
Ivy (marketing): Thanks team  aiming to freeze copy by EOD tomorrow so design can mock slides.
